idea: Why a toilet may keep running
title: Is Your Toilet Secretly Wasting Water?
description: A running toilet is one of the most common household plumbing issues, and it can waste hundreds of gallons of water each week. Usually, the culprit is inside the tank. A worn-out rubber flapper may no longer create a tight seal, allowing water to continuously trickle into the bowl. Alternatively, the float level might be set too high, sending excess water into the overflow tube. A misadjusted fill valve or a tangled chain can also prevent the mechanism from shutting off properly. While checking the flapper seal or chain is a great quick start, persistent leaks often require replacing internal hardware. If simple adjustments do not fix the issue, contact a licensed plumber to inspect and restore your system efficiently.
